items.prompt: Which word is spelt correctly?
hints: All four try to spell the same word.
Say it in parts: be, cause.
The end part is spelt c, a, u, s, e.
items.explanation: Because is spelt b, e, c, a, u, s, e.

options.why: This tricky word has au in the middle and ends with se.
Two letters are swapped.
The e at the end is missing.

items.prompt: Choose the missing word. 'I ___ swim when I was four.'
hints: When I was four is in the past.
The past of can is a tricky word.
It rhymes with would and should.
items.explanation: Could is the past of can. It is a tricky word with oul in the middle.

options.why: When I was four is in the past. Can is for now.
This is not how we spell it.
This is not how we spell it.

items.prompt: Write the missing letters. 'My best fr___nd is Lea.'
hints: Read the sentence. What is the word?
Two vowels are missing.
Remember: a friend is there to the end.
items.explanation: Friend is spelt f, r, ie, n, d.

items.prompt: Which word is the opposite of young?
hints: All four words share the same last three letters.
Young means not many years.
Think of your grandparents.
items.explanation: Old is the opposite of young. Cold, gold and hold have the same spelling pattern.

options.why: Cold is about how hot or cold something is.
Gold is a shiny yellow metal.
Hold means to keep in your hands.

items.prompt: Match the words that sound the same.
hints: Say each word out loud.
The words sound the same but are spelt differently.
Start with eye. Which word sounds just like it?
items.explanation: Would and wood, eye and I, hour and our, one and won sound the same but mean different things.

items.prompt: Choose the missing word. 'I have ___ apples.' (2)
hints: The number tells you which word.
Three of these words sound the same.
The number word has a silent w.
items.explanation: Two is the number 2. To and too sound the same but mean different things.

options.why: To is used in: I go to school.
Too means also, or very much.
Tow means to pull a car.

items.prompt: Choose all the words that are spelt correctly.
hints: Three words are right.
These words do not sound the way they are spelt.
Picture how each word looks in a book.
items.explanation: Water, again and busy are tricky words. They are spelt in ways you cannot fully hear.

options.why: Water is spelt w, a, t, e, r.
Again has ai: a, g, a, i, n.
Busy is spelt b, u, s, y.

items.prompt: Write the word that means 60 minutes. It starts with a silent h.
hints: Think about time words.
It sounds like our.
It starts with h, but you do not hear the h.
items.explanation: Hour means 60 minutes. The h is silent, so it sounds like our.

items.prompt: Which word has a silent letter?
hints: Say each word slowly.
A silent letter is written but not said.
Look at the end of each word.
items.explanation: Climb has a silent b at the end. We write it, but we do not say it.

options.why: You can hear every letter in clap.
You can hear every letter in club.
You can hear every letter in clip.

items.prompt: Sort the words. Do they have a silent letter?
hints: Say each word slowly.
Look for letters you cannot hear.
Start with knee. Do you hear the k?
items.explanation: Climb has a silent b, knee has a silent k and write has a silent w. You can hear every letter in jump, milk and lamp.

items.prompt: Which question word asks about a person?
hints: Think about the answer each word wants.
Which word could start: ___ is your teacher?
The answer would be a name.
items.explanation: Who asks about a person. Where asks about a place, when about time and what about a thing.

options.why: Where asks about a place.
When asks about time.
What asks about a thing.

items.prompt: Write the missing word. 'My mum and my ___ look after me.' It means dad and starts with f.
hints: Think of the grown-up word for dad.
It rhymes with rather.
It ends the same way as mother.
items.explanation: Father means dad. It is spelt f, a, t, h, e, r.

items.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
hints: Check each word carefully.
Many and children are tricky words.
Also check is or are.
items.explanation: Many is spelt with an a, children is the plural of child, and we say there are for more than one.

options.text: There are many children in the class.
There are meny children in the class.
options.why: Many is spelt m, a, n, y.

options.text: There are many childs in the class.
options.why: More than one child is children.

options.text: There is many children in the class.
options.why: For more than one, we use are.

items.prompt: Which word has the same vowel sound as child?
hints: Say child slowly.
The i in child says its name.
Find the word with a long i, like in kind.
items.explanation: Child and wild both have a long i. In will, chill and milk, the i is short.

options.why: Will has a short i.
Chill has a short i.
Milk has a short i.

items.prompt: Which word is the odd one out? 'great, break, steak, speak'
hints: Say each word out loud.
They all have ea, but ea can make different sounds.
Three of the words rhyme with make.
items.explanation: In great, break and steak, ea makes the long a sound. In speak, ea makes the long e sound.

options.why: Great has the same sound as break and steak.
Break has the same sound as great and steak.
Steak has the same sound as great and break.

items.prompt: How many words are spelt wrong? 'My frend sed we shud play agen.'
hints: Read each word one at a time.
Think of how each tricky word looks in a book.
Check frend first. Is it spelt right?
items.explanation: Frend, sed, shud and agen are wrong. They should be friend, said, should and again.

options.why: Check every word slowly.
Check the last word too.
My, we and play are spelt correctly.

items.prompt: Write the missing letters. 'She has a very pr___ty dress.'
hints: Read the sentence. What is the word?
It sounds like it has an i, but it does not.

items.explanation: Pretty is spelt p, r, e, t, t, y. It sounds like pritty, but it has an e.
